text:
Score: **6/10**. The code is small, readable, dependency-light, and the current tests pass (`12 passed`). I found no obvious command injection, secret handling, or unsafe deserialization issues. The main risk is data correctness: failed ingests can still mutate the database, timestamps are stored in forms SQLite compares incorrectly, and stale snapshots can overwrite newer terminal job states.

I would **not approve this as-is** for a production PR.

| Severity | Location | Issue |
|---|---:|---|
| high | [src/jobwatch/cli.py](/work/src/jobwatch/cli.py:83) lines 83-98 | Ingest writes valid rows before enforcing the malformed-row threshold, so a command that exits nonzero still partially mutates the database. |
| high | [src/jobwatch/parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:109), [src/jobwatch/store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:114) lines 109-125; 114,130,161,177-205 | ISO timestamps are stored as arbitrary strings and compared lexicographically, which breaks filtering/newest-window logic for timezone-aware or mixed timestamp formats. |
| medium | [src/jobwatch/store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:61) lines 61-73 | Unconditional upsert lets older snapshots regress completed/failed jobs back to stale running or pending states. |
| medium | [src/jobwatch/store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:11) lines 11,123-165 | Failure reporting only recognizes `FAILED`, `TIMEOUT`, and `OOM`, missing common Slurm failure states such as `OUT_OF_MEMORY`, `CANCELLED`, `NODE_FAIL`, and `PREEMPTED`. |
| medium | [src/jobwatch/cli.py](/work/src/jobwatch/cli.py:77) lines 77-87,108-112,127-132,161-165 | File/database errors outside parser validation are uncaught, so unreadable input, bad DB paths, or SQLite failures produce tracebacks instead of clean CLI errors. |
| medium | [src/jobwatch/store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:18) lines 18-20 | The default local database is created with process umask defaults, which can leave job/user accounting data readable by other local users. |
| low | [src/jobwatch/parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:91) lines 91-106 | GPU TRES parsing accepts negative counts and any key starting with `gres/gpu`, allowing malformed TRES data to corrupt usage totals. |
| low | [src/jobwatch/parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:182) lines 182-186 | Header validation requires an exact ordered field list, making the importer brittle to harmless `sacct` column-order or extra-column variations. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change scope: **160 lines**. That includes transactional ingest validation, timestamp normalization/query changes, safer upsert semantics, broader state classification, CLI error handling, DB permissions, parser hardening, and focused tests for those paths.

issues.description: Ingest writes valid rows before enforcing the malformed-row threshold, so failed ingests still partially mutate the database.
Timestamps are stored as arbitrary ISO strings and compared lexicographically, breaking filters and newest-window logic for timezone-aware or mixed formats.
Unconditional upsert lets stale snapshots overwrite newer terminal job states.
Failure reports miss common Slurm failure states such as OUT_OF_MEMORY, CANCELLED, NODE_FAIL, and PREEMPTED.
Unhandled file and SQLite errors can crash the CLI with tracebacks instead of user-facing errors.
The default SQLite database is created with umask-dependent permissions that may expose accounting data to other local users.
GPU TRES parsing accepts negative counts and overly broad gres/gpu-prefixed keys.
Exact ordered header validation makes ingestion brittle to harmless sacct column variations.
